inspectionBasis: Manual inspection of the exact source and all six matched textured orbit views for both routes.
campaignVerdict: Stable Fast 3D is a useful source-fidelity counter-route, especially for rigid or stylized component masses. Trellis remains the stronger whole-object coherence route for the ornate and organic cells in this assay.

rigid-stone-slabs.visibleReason: SF3D preserves the source's stocky silhouette, broad torso, and thick overlapping stone masses. Trellis keeps a more explicitly separable armor grammar but normalizes the body toward a leaner articulated creature.
rigid-stone-slabs.residualRisk: SF3D softens some plate boundaries and fuses local structure; this is a source-fidelity preference, not mechanical or production admission.

ornate-dragon.visibleReason: Trellis produces a substantially more coherent all-around dragon with reliable limbs, horns, tail, and dorsal structure. SF3D remains attractive near the conditioned view but its far-side horn, feet, and body junctions are less trustworthy.
ornate-dragon.residualRisk: Trellis changes source proportions and surface organization more strongly; preference is for whole-object coherence, not one-to-one source identity.

organic-skin.visibleReason: Trellis completes a more coherent organism across hidden views. SF3D stays somewhat closer to the visible source proportions but loses authority around the hidden face, ears, distal limbs, and bilateral completion.
organic-skin.residualRisk: Neither route is admitted for rigging or anatomical fidelity; Trellis wins only this source-specific usable-geometry comparison.
